title: plugin-charts: categorical x-axis above 5 buckets still loses labels (minTickGap)
body:
Fixes #7386

## What changed

`AdvancedChartImpl`'s `xAxisCommonProps` charged every categorical (bar/line/
area/combo) x-axis above `X_AXIS_ALL_LABELS_MAX_BUCKETS` (5 buckets) a
`minTickGap` of 48px (32px on mobile). `minTickGap` is **added on top of**
recharts' own measured-overlap check (`getTicks.js`: `start = tickCoord +
size/2 + minTickGap`), so this was mandatory whitespace beyond what real
collision avoidance already required — a time-series budget charged to band
axes too. A 7-status pipeline at a 290px widget (≈33px/band) dropped 4 of its
7 names even though nothing was actually wide enough to collide.

`minTickGap` is now `0` for that branch. `interval: 'preserveStartEnd'` is
unchanged, so recharts' own measured-width overlap avoidance is the only
thing governing tick density above the bound — the same mechanism that
already governed every tick it kept.

Not changed, and out of scope for this issue:
- `X_AXIS_ALL_LABELS_MAX_BUCKETS` / the ≤5-bucket "draw everything" branch
  (objectui#7247).
- The scatter chart's own `minTickGap={isMobile ? 32 : 48}`, on its XAxis
  where `type` is set to the string NUMBER — a genuinely continuous numeric
  measure axis, not a categorical band axis (scatter is explicitly excluded
  from `CATEGORY_AXIS_CHART_TYPES`), so the time-series-style budget is
  correctly scoped there and untouched.
- recharts' angled-tick collision model (`getAngledRectangleWidth`), which
  stays on its conservative projected-bounding-box approximation rather than
  the true parallel-line perpendicular-separation constraint. Documented in
  code as a deliberate choice, not an oversight — reimplementing that
  geometry is a bigger, untested-in-this-repo change than this issue's scope
  warrants.

## Why `minTickGap: 0` is not an arbitrary density pick

The issue's own diagnosis is that recharts "does not need the help" — it
already refuses to draw ticks whose measured boxes would overlap. `0` is not
a re-tuned density value; it is the literal removal of the extra margin,
leaving the pre-existing (and already-correct) measured-overlap check to do
all the work, exactly as it already does for the ticks it keeps.

## Real-browser verification (required — this repo's DOM test env cannot exercise it)

happy-dom's `getStringSize` reports `{width: 0, height: 0}` for every string,
so recharts' measured-overlap check cannot fire in this repo's unit tests at
all — the jsdom tests added/changed below can only prove the artificial floor
is gone, never that real text still avoids colliding. Verified instead with a
real-Chromium harness (React + recharts 3.10.1 built via esbuild, driven with
Playwright against the repo's own bundled Chromium), reproducing
`ChartContainerImpl`'s actual `text-xs` sizing and `apps/console`'s actual
`body` font stack (font-family/letter-spacing) — without which recharts'
hidden text-measurement span mismeasures against the wrong font entirely; see
#9430, filed out of scope, found while building this harness.

Overlap was checked as true rotated-rectangle intersection (SAT, via each
tick's `getCTM()`-mapped corners) — not an axis-aligned
`getBoundingClientRect()` box, which over-reports collisions for diagonal
text (confirmed by screenshot: an axis-aligned check flagged "overlaps" that
were not visually present).

| case | width | buckets | before (minTickGap 48) | after (minTickGap 0) | overlaps after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bar, rotated | 290px | 7 | 3/7 labels | **7/7 labels** | 0 |
| bar, rotated | 290px | 8 | 3/8 labels | **8/8 labels** | 0 |
| bar, rotated | 290px | 10 | 3/10 labels | 5/10 labels | 0 |
| bar, rotated | 200px | 7 | 2/7 labels | **4/7 labels** | 0 |
| line, dates | 200px | 24 | 2/24 labels | 3/24 labels | 0 |
| line, dates | 800px | 180 | 7/180 labels | 11/180 labels | 0 |

The last row is the regression check for the scenario the file's own comment
worries about ("hundreds of points painted a dense black bar"): thinning is
still very much in effect (11 of 180), and still zero-overlap — because
`minTickGap: 0` removes only the extra margin, not recharts' measured-width
check itself.

## Tests

- `packages/plugin-charts/src/AdvancedChartImpl.categoricalAxisDensity.test.tsx`
  — added 7-bucket/290px (the issue's own reproduction) and 6-bucket/200px
  cases asserting every label now draws; the pre-existing "still thins a
  high-cardinality axis" pin is rewritten (with an explanatory comment) since
  happy-dom's zero text metrics mean `minTickGap: 0` shows every tick
  regardless of count in THIS environment — the real safety property for
  that scenario is the 180-point/800px row above, which jsdom cannot exercise
  either way.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-charts test` — full package suite.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-charts type-check`.
- `packages/plugin-charts/src/ChartRenderer.catalogRender-6939.test.tsx`
  (maintainer ruling 5510084784, byte-identical render pin) — confirmed
  unaffected: both catalog fixtures have exactly 6 data points at the test's
  mocked 480px width, where 480/6 ≈ 80px per band already exceeded the OLD
  48px `minTickGap`, so all 6 ticks already drew under both old and new code.

## Acceptance notes

No findings withheld.

- The one adjacent thing that looked like a reproducible defect, found while
  building the real-browser harness: recharts' tick-size measurement span
  inherits `document.body`'s font-family rather than the chart's own, so a
  host page whose body font differs from the chart's silently mis-measures
  tick overlap. Separate, unassigned, out-of-scope: filed as #9430.
- An observation, not filed: the horizontal-bar family's category axis (the
  YAxis in the `isHorizontal` branch) formats its ticks with `xTickFormatter`
  directly rather than `xAxisTickFormatter`, so it never gets the ≤5-bucket
  rotated-label ellipsis objectui#7247 gave the vertical-bar path. Possibly
  deliberate — that axis already grows its own width from the longest label
  instead of rotating — so this is recorded as an asymmetry, not asserted as
  a bug.
